transcript.text: Thank you, Mara. Here's my accessibility update. I confirmed with the accessibility vendor this afternoon that the theater's approved service for The Glass Harbor is live audio description delivered through exactly 20 headsets. The reason for this approach is that projected captions would obstruct the restored intertitle image, which is a key artistic element of this silent film. I want to flag that this vendor confirmation is currently still in my accessibility file rather than in the event sheet, and it needs to be entered before I can provide my accessibility sign-off. I also see several intersections: Jon's 1.5-meter clear aisle constraint may be relevant to headset distribution logistics, and the audio description service is a live element that would need to fit within Victor's 6:30 to 7:45 PM window. Additionally, since Leila has confirmed the license prohibits any recording, that's consistent with our live-only audio description approach — there's no conflict there, but it's worth noting the accessibility service is also a live-only element.
